definition: Remiss means negligent; careless about a duty.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word remiss. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know remiss should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Aunt Rosa never let a birthday pass unmarked, and she scolded herself as remiss if a card arrived even one day late.
Careless is milder than remiss — general sloppiness, crumbs on the counter and a mislaid pen, with no particular duty attached, while remiss pins one neglected duty on one person.
Reckless goes further than remiss — remiss lets a duty quietly slide, while reckless charges ahead in a way that courts real harm.

Lax describes loose standards in general — a lax office, lax security, a whole regime gone soft about its rules. Remiss is narrower and more pointed: one specific duty existed, one answerable person let it slide, and the word politely hands them the blame.

Slack is the informal word for effort gone soft across the board — a slack week, slack attendance, energy sagging everywhere at once. Remiss never describes the general mood: it names one neglected obligation and quietly points at the person who owed it.

For thirty years the harbormaster at Dunmore raised the storm cones himself, two black triangles that told every skiff in the bay to run for shelter.
The morning of the October gale, the cones never went up.
An inquiry later established that the duty belonged to him alone and had been written into his contract since 1988.
Three boats were caught outside the breakwater; all three crews were pulled from the water, soaked and furious.
The board's report used one careful word: the harbormaster had been remiss.
Not corrupt, not malicious -- he had simply let the single task that mattered most slide on the one morning it mattered.
He accepted the finding without argument, and for the rest of his tenure the cones went up even for squalls that never arrived.
